executiveSummary: GM1842 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but it is not a calibrated Midden-Delfland first-72-hour forecast. This low polder municipality sits in Delfland's coupled polder/boezem system: higher urban and greenhouse areas can drain toward the boezem while lower Midden-Delfland depends on pumps with finite capacity, and official regional evidence makes both extreme rainfall and deep coastal inundation plausible. The model nevertheless reports exact T+24 river and coastal legacy flood amplitudes of 1.442150 and 1.854071, 11,305 and 12,151 affected people-equivalent, and exact service percentages without a named water body, boundary condition, defence/breach state, connected footprint, pump/boezem state or operator evidence. Eight unrelated non-compound hazards also reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood ranking. Public water assets, routes, utility planning, antennas, schools and hospitals are valuable context, but their missing capacity, current state and recovery data remain Unknown, never zero, safe or available. Unsupported physical and service precision must be suppressed or replaced, and first-72-hour actions need an authority-aware auditable ledger.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM1842 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM1842 as Midden-Delfland and report 19,423 residents, density 412 per square kilometre, 22.1% aged 65 or older and 2,342 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable fields retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [4.311678935338399, 51.971169408387155] and the BAG place points for Den Hoorn, Maasland and Schipluiden lie inside the 2025 generalized boundary. BRT adds seven smaller named settlements: 't Woudt, De Kapel, Gaag, Hodenpijl, Negenhuizen, Ter Lucht and Zouteveen.

Thirteen neighbourhood rows sum to 19,430 people, seven above the municipal total (+0.036%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 19,423. Registers omit event-time commuters, visitors, livestock, care dependency and household supplies.

evidenceSources.title: Wateroverlast, overstromingen and household preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The municipality says intense rain can exceed sewer capacity and flood streets, tunnels and cycle paths; it separates rainwater, uses ditches and temporary storage, and describes a Den Hoorn road construction that temporarily stores and releases rainwater. These are mechanisms and measures, not a live drainage state or municipal flood raster.

The official flood page at https://www.middendelfland.nl/overstromingen distinguishes sea/river/lake or defence flooding from rainfall nuisance, says impacts depend on breach location, velocity, depth and terrain, and explains that the public risk map is a maximum scenario assuming no intervention.

The same page warns that substantial flooding can disable electricity and likely water, gas and sewer services and damage roads and bridges. This is public preparedness guidance, not an operator fragility curve. It asks residents to be self-reliant for the first three days, including three litres of drinking water per person per day, but does not measure actual household stock or promise recovery at T+72.

evidenceSources.title: Delfland polder-boezem operation, candidate water storage and 2025–2030 cooperation
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; planning decision 9 April 2026; no blanket page licence identified
supports: Delfland explains that water from higher Westland and Den Haag can drain freely into the boezem while lower areas must pump into it; pump capacity is finite and this can raise water levels in lower Midden-Delfland. Local pluvial risk is therefore a coupled catchment, pump, storage and boezem problem, not a municipal scalar.

The Klaas Engelbrechtspolder and Woudse Polder were selected for further elaboration as strategic storage, with design figures of about 850,000 and 500,000 cubic metres. Realisation is estimated at 8–15 years and is not complete operational capacity; storage use also requires notification and moving livestock.

Delfland says storage does not prevent every water-on-street event and combines holding, storing, discharging, accepting/consequence reduction and spatial allocation. The municipality-Delfland partnership runs through 2030 and addresses wet winters, dry summers, water quality and peat meadow issues; it is governance context, not an event observation.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Haaglanden 2023 and appendices
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023; policy scenario evidence, not observation or forecast; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The regional profile places Haaglanden in former dike ring 14, identifies coastal flooding as the region's most relevant flood pathway, and specifically lists Midden-Delfland among municipalities with the greatest maximum inundation depths; extreme scenarios span roughly 0.5 to 5 metres depending on location and scenario.

It separately describes failure of regional boezem embankments, with local decimetre flooding, and notes that heavy rain following drought can increase breach risk. It also identifies intense rainfall as material in Westland and Midden-Delfland. These are scenario families, not proof that a breach or depth is active at the exercise clock.

The profile finds no regional areas expected to reach Mercalli VI or higher and treats relevant local induced events as very unlikely/limited. Nature-fire load is regionally limited, while smoke and cross-boundary toxic plumes can still matter. This supports hazard-specific mechanisms rather than one shared neighbourhood rank.

evidenceSources.title: NWB roads, A4 Ketheltunnel context, rail and scheduled public transport
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026 under CC0; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; current RWS tunnel page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Monthly NWB geometry produces seven logical cross-boundary links: A4 toward Rijswijk and Schiedam, A20 toward Vlaardingen and Westland, N211 and N223 toward Westland, and N470 toward Delft. A4/A20 paired links are series sections of physical corridors; generalized capacities are non-additive scenario ceilings, not measured emergency throughput.

Rijkswaterstaat states at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/wegen/wegenoverzicht/a4/ketheltunnel-a4 that the A4 runs half-sunken through Midden-Delfland and the downstream two-kilometre Ketheltunnel in Schiedam is controlled continuously from Rhoon. Static geometry and control responsibility do not establish event-time passability.

No ProRail station lies in GM1842; 20 GTFS stop areas serve its villages. Scheduled stops and absent bounded NDW records do not prove operation, evacuation throughput, bridge/tunnel status, road openness, fuel, staff or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Public water assets, grid planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 487 GM1842 context points: 3 sewer pumps, 6 sluices, 126 surface-water pumps, 1 wastewater treatment point and 351 weirs. Capacity is null for 442 points; points and remaining values do not establish units, hydraulic connectivity, operation, backup, redundancy or spare capacity.

A single NBNL sample at postcode 2636GB is assigned to De Lier/Westland and publishes zero queued requests at that sampled station plus planning capacities and no projects. That scoped published zero is not municipality-wide absence of congestion, current electricity availability, load, switching ability or restoration. The exact reuse licence for NBNL planning was not identified.

RDI returns 47 antenna records, including 11 mobile and 15 fixed-link sites; DUO returns 12 education records. Neither register establishes power/backhaul/coverage, shelter role, occupancy, supplies or event-time availability.

No acute-care department lies in GM1842. RIVM's annual CC0 questionnaire places the nearest reference-point facilities at Reinier de Graaf Delft (3.419 km straight-line, 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics), Franciscus Vlietland (7.154 km, limited-hours SEH) and Haga Leyweg (10.050 km, 24/7). These are not ambulance travel times, live acceptance, capacity, staffing, backup endurance or access.

evidenceSources.title: Emergency support point pilot and GHOR multi-year policy 2026–2030
evidenceSources.edition: Pilot advice and policy documents published 2026; planning/governance evidence, no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The regional emergency-support-point design uses a cross-provincial power outage lasting up to 72 hours, including potential telecom loss and limited self-reliance, and expects municipalities to establish initial public contact points in the first hours. It remains a pilot/design, not a guaranteed inventory of operating GM1842 sites.

GHOR Haaglanden's 2026–2030 plan aims to keep its own primary processes functioning for at least 72 hours and highlights vulnerable groups and emergency support points. A policy target is not measured facility autonomy, generator fuel, staff, medicines, water or local service restoration.
No reviewed public source supplies a current GM1842 action, staffing, stock, acceptance or completion feed. Absent action state must remain Unknown.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM1842 is uniquely Midden-Delfland in Zuid-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Haaglanden.
The reference point and three BAG place points are contained by the generalized 2025 boundary.
Annual statistics, current planning pages, register snapshots and the synthetic exercise clock retain separate valid times.

geography.summary: Municipal geometry is coherent, but hydrological exposure requires explicit polder, boezem, defence and source-water geometry.
notes: Two districts, 13 neighbourhoods, three BAG places and ten BRT settlements load coherently.
Higher Westland/Den Haag drainage, finite polder pumps, Delfland boezem levels, regional embankments and dike-ring/coastal pathways cross municipal boundaries.

A generic shoreline or elevation proxy cannot identify a breach-connected footprint, arrival, recession or pluvial pathway; each layer needs version, resolution, scenario, coverage, licence and NoData.

demography.summary: Official 2025 headline totals agree and small neighbourhood rounding is explicit.
notes: Population is 19,423, density 412, age65Pct 22.1 and one-person households 2,342.
Neighbourhood rows sum to 19,430 (+7, +0.036%) and allocation reconciles exactly to 19,423; households sum to 8,130 and published age65+ rows to 4,300.
Largest neighbourhoods are Den Hoorn 8,210, Maasland 4,585, Schipluiden 3,445 and Dijkpolder 1,185; registers omit transient and institution populations.

regionalDetail.summary: All neighbourhoods load, but socioeconomic, hydraulic and operational detail remains incomplete.
notes: Home-value/housing/tenure fields exist for 11/13 neighbourhoods; cars per household for 8/13; benefit fields for 12/13; district heating and public charging for 0/13. Null is not zero.
Of 487 HWH water points, 442 have null capacity; remaining values cannot be aggregated without units, topology and state.
NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records are static/planning context, not incident-time availability.

settlements.summary: Den Hoorn, Maasland, Schipluiden and seven smaller BRT settlements are spatially coherent.
notes: BAG place points are contained and no settlement identity mismatch was found.
The smaller settlements matter for dispersed access, warning, agricultural/livestock action and supply but labels do not quantify those needs.
NoData for event-time occupancy, reception or self-reliance remains Unknown.

transport.summary: A4/A20 and provincial corridors are reproducible, while internal bridges, half-sunken roads and destination access remain unresolved.
notes: Seven logical cross-boundary edges reach Delft, Rijswijk, Schiedam, Vlaardingen and Westland; A4/A20 paired segments are non-additive.
The half-sunken A4 and downstream Ketheltunnel create relevant access dependencies, but no reviewed feed proves current passability or control state.
There is no local rail station; 20 scheduled stop areas do not establish operation. Internal polder roads, bridges and hospital routes require explicit incident state.

emergencyContext.summary: Official roles and 72-hour guidance exist, but no auditable local action/resource/acceptance state drives the simulator.
notes: Delfland, municipality, safety region, Rijkswaterstaat, road operators, utilities and GHOR have distinct roles that are not represented as triggers, assignments, resources, status or completion.
No acute-care department is local; Delft, Schiedam and Den Haag capacity depends on cross-boundary route, acceptance, staffing and utilities that remain Unknown.

Required first-72-hour categories include warning, polder/boezem and defence decisions, livestock movement, village welfare checks, tunnel/bridge/road control, medical transport, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.
Household preparedness guidance and a regional support-point pilot are not inventories or recovery guarantees.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: The mandatory gate covers severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Affected people-equivalent is not observed people, casualties or evacuees; person-hours is cumulative weighted local service shortfall against a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: The initial focused GM1842 model gate passed both tests over the complete matrix.
Intensity-zero effects, repeatability, UI/core preset equality, local allocation, route ceilings, hazard-layer invariance and event-attributable burden contracts pass.
Numerical correctness does not establish local calibration or operational validity.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Exact flood amplitudes and one repeated neighbourhood order are not derived from Midden-Delfland's hazard pathways.
notes: Coastal T+24 reports legacy flood amplitude 1.854071 and 12,151 affected people-equivalent without a selected sea level, source water body, defence/breach state, connected footprint or arrival/recession.
River T+24 reports 1.442150 and 11,305 affected and remains exactly at that severity, amplitude, affected count and service state through T+72 without a named river or defence scenario.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire all rank the complete 13-neighbourhood set identically; the top five are Verspreide huizen Duifpolder en omgeving, Schipluiden, Dijkpolder, Verspreide huizen Schipluiden and Gaag-Maasland.
Some top-ranked low polders may be relevant to water hazards, but exact reuse by heat, cyber, winter, storm and wildfire proves that ranking is not hazard-specific causality.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service values are inspectable but unsupported by Delfland, utility, transport or care evidence.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 0.334026, water 0.382329, drainage 0.263481, gas 0.665499, telecom 0.336858, mobility 0.714026, facilities 0.336937 and supply 0.368581; no operator validates those values.
The 487 water points, one grid-planning sample, 47 antennas, 12 education records and external hospitals remain non-causal context.
A4/A20, bridges, tunnel control, bus operation, hospital acceptance and utility interdependence are not represented by time-stamped operational state.
Unavailable or security-sensitive topology requires explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, not invented asset precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes exist, but unresolved event, defence, target and operational dimensions are hidden.
notes: River/coastal are labelled derived-screening yet show unsupportedDimensions=[] despite absent source water, boundary hydrograph/level and datum, wind, defence/breach/overtopping state, footprint, arrival and recession.
A legacy field named floodDepthM must not be presented as surveyed or forecast metres.
Static registers, current pages, long-horizon projects, official scenario libraries and synthetic output have different valid times and evidence classes.
Cyber requires a named target and confirmed dependency; empty local observations or missing operational fields become Unknown, not inferred normality.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 residuals and plateaus have no event, operator, dewatering, care or action evidence.
notes: River remains unchanged from T+24 to T+72 at severity 0.456369, legacy flood amplitude 1.442150, affected 11,305 and pressure 0.553136 while person-hours rise to 714,121.131.

Coastal direct severity and legacy amplitude clear to zero by T+72, but 4,052 affected people-equivalent and 715,530.410 person-hours remain; no recession, pump/dewatering, route or repair evidence supports that trajectory.
Compound T+72 retains legacy flood amplitude 0.270909, affected 12,982 and pressure 0.614413; all eight service values are exactly unchanged from T+24, while person-hours rise to 768,982.487.
A 72-hour self-reliance horizon and policy target do not establish restoration, facility autonomy, support-point availability or household stock.

findings.summary: The coastal preset exposes plausible risk with unsupported event and depth precision.
findings.evidence: VR Haaglanden identifies potentially deep coastal inundation in Midden-Delfland, but the model's T+24 legacy amplitude 1.854071 and 12,151 affected people-equivalent have no named source water, sea level/datum, wind, primary-defence/breach state or connected footprint.
findings.action: Suppress precise direct impact until a selected versioned LIWO/authority scenario supplies source water, boundary condition, defence state, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Nonzero possibility must remain Unknown rather than be forced to zero.

findings.summary: The river preset shows a persistent major flood without a named river pathway.
findings.evidence: River severity 0.456369, amplitude 1.442150, 11,305 affected and all service states remain exactly unchanged from T+24 through T+72. The regional profile identifies coastal flooding as most relevant and separately discusses regional boezem-embankment breaches; neither validates this unnamed river state.
findings.action: Require a selected major-river source, boundary hydrograph, defence/breach state and hydraulic footprint before direct river effects. Keep major-river, coastal and Delfland boezem/polder breach scenarios separate and mark unresolved effects Unknown.

findings.summary: One neighbourhood multiplier drives eight unrelated hazards.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the exact same complete 13-neighbourhood order and same top five, including dispersed Duifpolder first. This cannot simultaneously encode drainage, defence, heat, cyber, wind and smoke pathways.
findings.action: Remove the shared ranking from physical impact. Integrate source-specific hazard surfaces and exposure, or render municipal amplitude uniformly/Unknown; add tests for cross-hazard rank diversity and tie handling.

findings.summary: Pluvial output omits the coupled Delfland polder-boezem and sewer mechanism.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports amplitude 0.223411 and mobility 0.356024 without rainfall hyetograph, AHN/BGT flow paths, sewer inclusion, soil/groundwater saturation, pump state, boezem level or upstream Westland/Den Haag drainage. Official Delfland evidence says these interactions are material.
findings.action: Integrate a versioned municipal/Delfland stress-test or 3Di-style result with rainfall, terrain, sewer-included flag, pump/boezem boundary conditions, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Do not use planned storage volume as current capacity.

findings.summary: Exact utility and recovery percentages have no operator or hydraulic evidence.
findings.evidence: The model emits eight precise coastal availability values and deterministic residual curves. HWH points, an NBNL sample, antennas, road geometry and public hospital registers provide no live outage, topology, switching, backup, fuel, repair or restoration state.
findings.action: Keep public context affectsSimulation=false and label operational values aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Accept only authorized time-scoped operator or authority aggregates, with manual incident overrides retaining author, timestamp, scope and expiry.

findings.summary: Delfland water points are useful context but mostly capacity-Unknown and non-operational.
findings.evidence: The deployment contains 487 HWH assets, of which 442 have null capacity; point type, location and manager do not establish units, catchment connectivity, status, redundancy or spare capacity.
findings.action: Retain source collection, point geometry, manager, nulls, licence, retrieval and coverage. Seek Delfland-authorized catchment/control aggregates; never sum incomparable fields or turn absent Waterinfo/state into zero or safe.

findings.summary: The boundary road graph misses critical internal and downstream access state.
findings.evidence: Seven NWB logical links capture A4/A20/N211/N223/N470, while A4 is half-sunken and depends downstream on the remotely controlled Ketheltunnel. Internal polder roads, bridges, live passability, public-transport operation and routes to external hospitals remain unresolved.
findings.action: Retain NWB only for mobility/supply with non-additive corridor semantics. Add named critical crossings/destinations and official live road/rail feeds where available; otherwise show passability and acceptance Unknown.

findings.summary: External acute care is not modelled as a route-dependent first-72-hour service.
findings.evidence: GM1842 has no acute-care department. Annual RIVM data identify nearby Delft, Schiedam and Den Haag facilities, but straight-line distance and opening classification do not establish ambulance time, diversion, capacity, staffing, backup utilities, supplies or flood-accessible routes.
findings.action: Represent external facility role, live acceptance/diversion, transport route, backup/fuel, critical supplies and mutual aid only from authorized time-scoped feeds; all absent fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Derived-screening labels conceal unsupported flood and operational dimensions.
findings.evidence: River/coastal claim unsupportedDimensions=[] while missing the event selections needed to interpret depth and affected counts. Planning pages, official scenarios, registers and synthetic trajectories are presented alongside one exercise clock without adequate validity separation.
findings.action: Populate unsupported dimensions and show them beside maps, briefs and exports. Preserve publisher, version, retrieval, valid/event time, evidence class, licence, coverage, spatial resolution, NoData and affectsSimulation for every layer.

findings.summary: No auditable action/resource ledger covers the first 72 hours.
findings.evidence: Official sources describe municipality, Delfland, safety-region, road, utility and GHOR responsibilities, household guidance, moving livestock before storage use and emergency-support-point development. The model has no local trigger, authority, assignment, resource, status or completion evidence.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first checkpoint records for warning, defence/polder/boezem decisions, pump/storage use, livestock movement, dispersed-village welfare, road/bridge/tunnel control, medical transport, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.

corrections.summary: Replace unsupported GM1842 coastal and river forcing with explicit source-water and defence-event semantics.
corrections.validation: Without a selected named authority scenario, GM1842 direct coastal/river impact is unsupported/Unknown and no exact depth or affected count is shown; fixtures preserve source water, boundary condition, defence state, footprint, timing, version, licence, coverage and NoData.

corrections.summary: Remove the shared neighbourhood rank and integrate hazard-specific coastal, river and pluvial geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated hazards no longer share the same complete neighbourhood order; water fixtures distinguish primary-defence, regional-boezem breach and rainfall pathways and retain data coverage.

corrections.summary: Model Delfland polder, pump, storage and boezem boundary conditions without converting registry or planned values into live capacity.
corrections.validation: Pluvial runs identify rainfall, terrain, sewer flag, pump/boezem boundary, valid time and NoData; 442 null asset capacities and planned storage remain Unknown/non-operational.

corrections.summary: Keep water, grid, telecom, education, transport and acute-care context non-causal until authorized incident state exists.
corrections.validation: Cards/exports show provenance, valid time, licence, coverage and affectsSimulation=false; missing observations, passability, capacity, acceptance and restoration never render as zero, safe, open or available.

corrections.summary: Implement a role-aware Unknown-first GM1842 first-72-hour action and resource ledger.
corrections.validation: At each checkpoint, water/defence, livestock, welfare, transport, care, water distribution, reception/resupply and repair actions show authority, trigger, assignment, resource, state, source/valid time and completion; absent facts remain Unknown and only confirmed actions affect recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish electricity, gas, drinking-water, telecom, sewer or Delfland operational topology, current control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Flood consequence depends on a named source water, boundary hydrograph/level, wind, primary or regional defence state, connected footprint, pump/boezem operation, arrival and recession; regional maximum scenarios and planning pages are not live forecasts.
HWH completeness varies, NBNL is one sampled planning point, and absent Waterinfo/NDW/local acute-care output is coverage—not normality, unconstrained capacity, open roads or safe conditions.
CBS/BAG/DUO/RIVM data omit visitors, commuters, agricultural workers/livestock, home-care needs, hospital occupancy, reception capacity and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuees, patients or customer interruptions.
Current weather, water, road, warning, utility and facility state can change after completion; stale or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Define Zuid-Holland coastal, Rhine/Meuse major-river and regional Delfland boezem/polder-breach scenarios as separate source-water/defence contracts rather than interchangeable flood presets.
Reconcile Midden-Delfland with Westland, Delft, Den Haag, Vlaardingen, Schiedam and Rijswijk using one versioned catchment/boezem, defence, pump and cross-boundary drainage evidence model.
Test the repeated neighbourhood-ranking defect across Zuid-Holland rural polders, dense urban areas, coast, heat, cyber and nature-fire contexts.
Audit A4/A20, Ketheltunnel, provincial roads, bridges, bus links and external hospital routes as non-additive, time-scoped access dependencies.
Treat Delfland asset nulls, planned storage and NBNL/RDI/RIVM registers consistently as context; public absence never means zero, safe, spare or available.

Require Unknown-first 72-hour action records for dispersed villages, livestock/agriculture, water management, care access, emergency support points, resupply and mutual aid across Haaglanden and Rotterdam-Rijnmond.
